claims.text: Using CALPHAD improves phase-stability prediction in high-entropy alloy design compared with traditional trial-and-error approaches.
Using CALPHAD in high-entropy alloy design produces refined microstructures compared with trial-and-error design.
Using CALPHAD in high-entropy alloy design optimizes material properties compared with trial-and-error design.
Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ti is a quinary system suitable as an example for CALPHAD-based high-entropy alloy exploration.
CALPHAD calculations require computational software and a thermodynamic database.
CALPHAD can be used to investigate composition and temperature effects relevant to high-entropy alloy microstructure.
Parallel computational capabilities can enhance CALPHAD-based alloy design.
Reliable thermodynamic data are necessary for accurate CALPHAD results.
CALPHAD predictions should be verified under experimental heat-treatment and solidification conditions.
CALPHAD predicts dominant phases such as BCC phases or intermetallic compounds.
CALPHAD-predicted phase-formation details mediate microstructural refinement.
CALPHAD computes free-energy differences among competing phases.
Computing free-energy differences enables prediction of phase equilibria and transformation pathways.
CALPHAD-guided compositional adjustment yields finer and more stable microstructures.
Finer and more stable microstructures optimize mechanical properties.
CALPHAD-designed alloys exhibit clearer phase distributions, smaller undesirable-phase fractions, refined features, and improved mechanical properties relative to empirically designed alloys.
The effectiveness of CALPHAD depends on the quality of the thermodynamic database.
CALPHAD calculations become computationally challenging for systems containing more than five elements unless adequate computational resources are available.
Quantitative improvements in phase stability and properties vary with the alloy system and database accuracy.
Experimental validation is necessary to establish the predicted improvements.
